description: Formula benchmark for the mathematical-extraction pipeline. Every item pairs (a) a source passage, (b) its verified mathematical interpretation and (c) the expected symbolic representation. Evaluation is split into five decoupled stages (see run_formula_eval.py): passage detection, formula retrieval, formula extraction, symbolic validity, interpretation correctness.
expr_convention: expected.expr is the canonical SymPy expression for the quantity (e.g. a**2, pi*r**2). Symbolic equivalence to the system's returned expression is tested with sympy.simplify(retrieved - expected) == 0. Relational statements (Pythagoras) are written in equal-to-zero form.

provenance_levels.verified_secondary: Verse identity and translation checked against a reliable secondary source (edition/encyclopaedia) during this work; Devanagari follows the standard received text.
provenance_levels.project_corpus: Passage comes from this project's own annotated data; the mathematical interpretation is asserted by the benchmark author and is NOT externally sourced.
provenance_levels.needs_review: Provenance or interpretation not yet confirmed; must be checked by a domain reviewer before publication.

items.query_text: दीर्घचतुरश्रस्याक्ष्णया रज्जुः पार्श्वमानी तिर्यग्मानी च यत्पृथग्भूते कुरुतस्तदुभयं करोति।
items.gloss: The rope stretched along the diagonal of a rectangle makes (an area) equal to that made by its length and breadth separately.

expected.name: Pythagorean theorem
expected.interpretation: The square on the diagonal equals the sum of the squares on the two sides.

provenance.notes: Devanagari matches the received verse quoted by Wikipedia/Baudhayana; translation via Sen & Bag (1983).

items.query_text: The diagonal of a square produces double the area of the square.
items.gloss: Diagonal-squared equals twice the side-squared for a square.

expected.name: Square-diagonal relation
expected.interpretation: In a square the square on the diagonal is twice the square on a side.

provenance.notes: Translation from Wikipedia (Shulba Sutras), citing Sen & Bag 1983. The system has no registry entry for this relation.

items.query_text: This is observed in rectangles having sides 3 and 4, 12 and 5, 15 and 8, 7 and 24, 12 and 35, 15 and 36.
items.gloss: List of Pythagorean triples used to set out right angles.

expected.name: Pythagorean triples
expected.interpretation: Enumerates integer right-triangle side triples (a^2 + b^2 = c^2).

provenance.notes: Detection-only item: mathematical content with no single formula to extract.

items.query_text: The measure is to be increased by its third and this again by its own fourth less the thirty-fourth part of that fourth; this is the value of the diagonal of a square whose side is the measure.
items.gloss: Rational approximation to sqrt(2): 1 + 1/3 + 1/(3*4) - 1/(3*4*34) = 577/408.

expected.name: Square-root-of-2 approximation
expected.interpretation: A rational approximation to the diagonal-to-side ratio of a square.

items.query_text: To transform a circle into a square, the diameter is divided into eight parts; one such part, after being divided into twenty-nine parts, is reduced by twenty-eight of them and further by the sixth of the part left less the eighth of the sixth part.
items.gloss: Squaring-the-circle construction giving pi approximately 3.088.

expected.name: Pi approximation (circle-square transformation)
expected.interpretation: A rule for squaring the circle that implies pi ~ 3.088.

items.gloss: The area of a triangle is the product of half the base and the perpendicular (height).

expected.name: Area of triangle
expected.interpretation: Area of a triangle equals half the product of base and height.

provenance.notes: The Wikisource index of the critical edition lists 'त्रिभुजस्य फलशरीरं (गणित 6 a)'; Devanagari follows the standard reading.

items.query_text: The area of a circle is equal to half the circumference multiplied by the radius.
items.gloss: Aryabhata's circle-area rule, equivalent to pi*r^2.

expected.name: Area of circle
expected.interpretation: Area of a circle is pi times the square of the radius.

provenance.notes: Content section verified from the Wikisource table of contents; exact verse number to be confirmed by a reviewer.

items.query_text: The sum of a series is the number of terms multiplied by half the sum of the first and last terms.
items.gloss: Arithmetic-series summation rule.

expected.name: Arithmetic series sum
expected.interpretation: Sum of an arithmetic series equals n(a+l)/2.

provenance.notes: Standard Aryabhatan result; exact verse reference to be confirmed.

items.gloss: The area of a square is the square of its side.

expected.name: Area of square
expected.interpretation: Area of a square equals the square of its side.

provenance.notes: Sample passage is not a critical-edition text; interpretation asserted by the benchmark author.

items.gloss: The area of a rectangle is its length multiplied by its breadth.

expected.name: Area of rectangle
expected.interpretation: Area of a rectangle equals length times breadth.

provenance.notes: The system's registry has no rectangle formula.

items.gloss: The area of a triangle is the base multiplied by half the altitude.

expected.name: Area of triangle
expected.interpretation: Area of a triangle equals half the base times the height.
